nodes.label: Achilles
nodes.description: Invulnerable everywhere but his heel because his mother Thetis (a Nereid, or water creature) held him by the heel to dip him in the magical River Styx when he was a baby.

edges.description: Agamemnon is king of the Achaeans, and he and Achilles have a disagreement that almost loses them the Trojan war. "Sing of it from the moment when Agamemnon, Atreus' son, that king of men, parted in wrath from noble Achilles."

Achilles left for his fine fleet and his huts, with Patroclus, son of Menoetius, and his men; while Agamemnon launched a swift ship in the waves, chose twenty oarsmen, and embarked an offering for the god, then sent the fair-faced daughter of Chryses aboard, with Odysseus, that man of resource, to take command.

But I say true, and swear a solemn oath See this staff, that will never leaf or sprout again now it is severed from its mountain branch, doomed never to be green again, stripped by the bronze adze of its foliage and bark, now borne in their hands by the Achaean judges who defend the laws of Zeus: I swear, on this, a solemn oath to you, that a day will surely come when the Achaeans, one and all, shall long for Achilles, a day when you, despite your grief, are powerless to help them, as they fall in swathes at the hands of man-killing Hector.
Tearfully, [Achilles] spoke, and his lady mother [Thetis] heard him, in the sea's depths, where she sat beside her aged father.
